analysis: Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md: a single table row added at head line 671 describing prompt-chunk attention (128-query blocks, a fused `.causal` path for eligible full-attention chunks, `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_FUSED_CAUSAL_PREFILL=0` to restore blocks). No source, config, key, endpoint, wire-contract, or deployment change is in this PR, so no control is weakened and no threat assumption is invalidated in the supplied evidence. I checked it against TB-007 (inference engine), T-028 (residual GPU data), T-041 (prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle), T-029 and the availability concerns. The row is descriptive: it covers attention scoring geometry, not cache scope, tenant isolation, SSD at-rest storage, KEK/HMAC lookup naming, TTL, or the cacheSalt plumbing that T-041 treats as sign-off-sensitive. The new env var is a performance/kill-switch knob. The existing deadline-qualification guard (`DeadlineRuntimeEnvironment.permitsQualification`, described at ~line 726) already rejects unrecognized or performance-affecting `DARKBLOOM_*` settings. I cannot verify that guard covers the new key, because the implementing code in AttentionV1.swift and PagedLayerCache.swift is not supplied. The fused-versus-block numerical difference could in principle affect output equivalence or timing, but that is an unverified implementation contract, not a documented regression. The rest of the file (Nemotron Super slot, MTP, deadlines, calibration) appears unchanged context. The unchanged text states bounded memory reservations, authenticated cache-scope partitioning and no cache receipts, none of which this PR alters. A later pass reviewing the implementing Swift change should confirm the fused path preserves paged-KV bounds, request isolation, and that the env var is covered by the qualification environment guard.
